name: Mamiya 6
note: 1989 interchangeable-lens 6×6 rangefinder — the record carries rangefinder/120/6×6 cm and a 1989 introduction, so this is the modern system body, not the pre-war fixed-lens folders sold as Mamiya Six. Three G-series lenses exist for it and were unreachable from the body without this mount.

name: Mamiya 7II
note: was format 35mm while carrying frame_size 6×7 cm — self-contradictory, and 35mm is impossible for a 6×7 frame. The 7II takes the same six-lens N/L range as the Mamiya 7.

name: Mamiya 645 AF
note: electronic autofocus mount, kept deliberately separate from the manual-focus Mamiya 645 — the two are not interchangeable in the way a shared 'Mamiya 645' value would imply.

name: Mamiya 645 AFD
note: represented as a fixed-lens camera with a fixed_lens named only 'Mamiya'. The 645 AFD is an interchangeable-lens medium-format SLR; the fixed_lens sub-object was a bad parse, not a fact.

name: Mamiya 645 AFDII
note: same electronic AF mount as the 645 AF/AFD generation.

name: Mamiya M645 Super, Pro, Pro TL and E
note: manual-focus 645 mount. The record covers the Super/Pro/Pro TL/E family under one name; they share the mount, so the correction holds for all of them.

name: Mamiya RB 67 Professional
note: spaced spelling of the RB67 Professional. Same bellows-focusing RB67 mount; never interchangeable with RZ67.

name: Mamiya RB 67 Pro S
note: spaced spelling of the RB67 Pro S. Same RB67 mount.

name: Mamiya RZ 67
note: spaced spelling of the RZ67. The RZ mount is electronic and distinct from the RB67 — the two lens lines must not merge.
